source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 3 (ISL A3) · lesson 13. Rewritten for children from Dr. Hassan's lesson; facts and references kept.

title.en: Hajj: the journey to Allah's House

learn.en: Ḥajj is the journey to the Kaʿbah in Makkah, in the month of Dhul-Ḥijjah. It is the fifth pillar of Islam. (Qur'an 3:97)
learn.title: The fifth pillar

learn.en: It is a must once in a lifetime for every grown-up Muslim who is able: healthy, with enough money, and a safe way to get there.
learn.title: Once in a lifetime

learn.en: Pilgrims put on iḥrām — men wear two plain white sheets — and call out the talbiyah: “Here I am, O Allah, here I am.”
learn.title: Iḥrām and talbiyah

learn.en: They walk around the Kaʿbah seven times (ṭawāf) and walk seven times between the hills of Ṣafā and Marwah (saʿy).
learn.title: Ṭawāf and saʿy

learn.en: On the 9th of Dhul-Ḥijjah they stand at ʿArafah — the heart of ḥajj. Then Muzdalifah, Minā, stoning the pillars, and Eid!
learn.title: The great day of ʿArafah

learn.en: “The reward of an accepted ḥajj is nothing less than Paradise.” (Bukhari 1773)
learn.title: The reward

words.en: Here I am, O Allah, here I am

quiz.en: How many times do pilgrims walk around the Kaʿbah?
What happens on the 9th of Dhul-Ḥijjah?
True or false? Ḥajj is a must every year.
True or false? The reward of an accepted ḥajj is Paradise.

move.en: Walk around a table seven times, like ṭawāf around the Kaʿbah!

think.q: If you could go to ḥajj one day, which part would you most like to see?
think.a: Maybe the Kaʿbah, ʿArafah, or drinking Zamzam — make du'aa that Allah lets you go!

parents.summary: Ḥajj, the fifth pillar, is once in a lifetime for those able. Pilgrims wear iḥrām, say the talbiyah, do ṭawāf and saʿy, and stand at ʿArafah. An accepted ḥajj's reward is Paradise.

try.en: Here I am, O Allah, here I am

parents.tip: Watch a short video of ṭawāf together and count the seven rounds.
